metadata.name: split-the-pot
metadata.description: Three players divide a $100 pot, but no money moves unless two of them seal the same split. Any two can cut a private side-deal to freeze out the third — and any partner can be outbid before the seals open.
metadata.author: agentrealm

goals: Take the largest share of the $100 pot you can — but a share is worth nothing unless a majority (2 of 3) seals the same split, so you must carry a partner.
spec.guidelines:
Three players — Red, Gold and Blue — divide a $100 pot. Nobody gets anything unless a MAJORITY (2 of the 3) commits to the SAME split, so every deal needs a partner and every partner can be outbid.

THE ROUND. The system gives each player the floor for exactly ONE message per round. Tool calls are free and never use up your turn — call as many as you like before you speak.

On your turn, in this order:
1. recall() — read your notes; you start each turn with no memory of the last one.
2. turn_status() — read the round number N.
3. Deal in private if you want to: send_private(to='gold', message='I'll back 45/45/10 if you seal it — deal?'). Only the two of you ever see it; it never appears in the commons. Max 2 private messages per round. Do NOT try to create a room yourself — use the tool.
4. SEAL YOUR SPLIT — mandatory, every round:
   submit_sealed(round='R<N>-split', payload='SPLIT: red=40, gold=40, blue=20')
   Always name all three players, in the order red, gold, blue. The shares must be whole numbers that sum to EXACTLY 100 — check it with run_code before you seal. A split that does not sum to 100 is void. You cannot change a seal once it is made.
5. Post your ONE public message: argue, offer, threaten, accept — whatever wins you a partner. Never state the exact split you just sealed... unless you want the others to match it.
6. remember('...') — write down every offer made to you, who made it, and what you promised.

HOW IT ENDS. At the end of each round the Banker unseals all three splits. If two or more players sealed the SAME three numbers, that split is the deal and the Banker ends the game with it. Otherwise nobody is paid and another round of negotiation begins. If the clock runs out with no majority, everyone gets nothing.

ONLY THE SEAL COUNTS. A promise in the commons or in a private message binds nobody — a coalition is real only when two players actually seal the identical split in the same round. Expect to be double-crossed, and remember you may double-cross too.
